binding_rules.rule: requested runtime_provider must match the registered binding
poll daemon_id must match the registered binding
poll runtime_id must match the registered binding
poll device_id must match only when the binding has a non-empty device_id

a daemon poll validates the current durable agent/runtime/device/daemon identity without applying time-based liveness projection; deleted, rebound, explicitly unavailable, or mismatched bindings remain rejected
nil registry imposes no binding gate

device_rules.rule: machine_id derives a stable physical-machine DeviceID
workspace connections are unioned across enroll/snapshot/connect paths
each authenticated account and workspace connection is preserved as a device grant without replacing device ownership or credentials
an agent created by a connected account routes through the existing physical daemon by stable device and runtime ids
snapshot restore backfills the original credential owner connection when older snapshots have no explicit grants
daemon agent-bindings include every agent whose verified runtime binding targets the device, even when the agent workspace is not in connected_workspace_ids
agentd-local runtimes are pruned from restored snapshots
runtime and daemon bindings remain live across two legacy heartbeat windows and become stale only after 45 seconds without a snapshot

source_checks.name: daemon-poll-durable-binding
contains: authenticated poll is fresh liveness evidence

loop.observation: A second account could connect to an existing physical daemon, while long-window testnet evidence still showed sporadic binding_agent_not_registered poll rejections whenever an otherwise valid daemon snapshot aged past the read-model liveness threshold.
loop.hypothesis: Stable physical identity, persisted account grants, and a daemon-poll-specific durable identity lookup can preserve security boundaries without treating an authenticated matching poll as an unregistered agent merely because its preceding snapshot is stale.
loop.execute: Persist connection grants, expose a semantic revision, backfill legacy snapshots, retain read-model liveness projection, and validate daemon polls against the current durable binding while rejecting explicit unavailability and identity mismatch.
loop.evaluate: The verifier and focused tests prove stable device/runtime ids, cross-account routing, credential survival, legacy backfill, stale read-model exclusion, successful matching polls across stale snapshots, and fail-closed mismatched or explicitly unavailable polls.
loop.retrospective: Registration identity and availability projection are different facts: UI and binding discovery remain time-sensitive, while a matching authenticated poll is itself liveness evidence and must be checked against durable identity rather than a stale projection.
